connector: Last week you read about who lived in a castle. Today: how a castle was built, stone by stone. Every wall, ditch and bridge had a reason. Look for the cause, why it was built that way, and the effect, what it did.

a.raw: the masons at conwy castle worked for king edward
a.why: The starts the sentence. Conwy Castle is the name of one castle, so both words get capitals. King is a title right before his name, Edward. A period ends the sentence.

b.raw: workers carried stone to dover castle in wooden carts
b.fixed: Workers carried stone to Dover Castle in wooden carts.
b.why: Workers starts the sentence, so it gets a capital W. Dover Castle is the name of one castle. A period ends the sentence.

vcloze1.h1: Find the word for a deep ditch full of water.
vcloze1.why: A moat is a deep ditch filled with water around a castle.

vcloze2.h1: This worker cuts and places stone. Look for stone inside the word.
vcloze2.why: A stonemason is a skilled worker who builds with stone.

vcloze3.h1: This bridge could be pulled up. Look for bridge inside the word.
vcloze3.why: A drawbridge could be raised so no one could cross the moat.

vcloze4.h1: Find the word for the strongest tower in the middle of the castle.
vcloze4.why: The keep was the strongest inner tower, the last place to defend.

glossary.m: what a whole paragraph is mostly about. It is often in the first sentence.
the sentence that tells the main idea of a paragraph, often the first one
one fact that helps prove the main idea
a sentence that does not help the main idea, so it does not belong in that paragraph
what happens because of a cause
a time in history about 500 to 1,500 years ago, when there were castles, knights and kings in Europe
the main word before an ending is added. Hope is the base word in hopeful.

cards.title: Job Spotlight: The Stonemason
cards.sub: A real job in the Middle Ages
cards.todo: Read about this real job. Then read the two questions and the article.
text: A stonemason cut big blocks of stone and fit them together to build walls and towers.
Masons learned the trade as apprentices, over many years.
Many masons carved their own mark into the stones they shaped. You can still find these marks in old castles and churches.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Last week you read about who lived in a castle. Today: how a castle was built. Look for the reason behind every wall and ditch.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first. A root that means write, main ideas and details, and four endings you know.
transcripts.guide2: Read how castles were built. Find one thing the builders did, and why.
transcripts.guide3: Today you write your whole paragraph.

notes.wordParts: The root script or scribe means write. describe = to write about something. manuscript = written by hand. One root, two spellings.
notes.grammar: A paragraph has one main idea, often in the first sentence (the topic sentence). The other sentences are details that support it. A sentence that does not support it is off the topic.
notes.spelling: -ful means full of (hopeful). -less means without (hopeless). -ness turns a describing word into a thing (kindness). -ly tells how something was done (quickly).
notes.wgrd: A cause is why something happens. The effect is what happens. Castles had thick walls because enemies attacked.
vocab: a deep ditch, often filled with water, around a castle
a skilled worker who cuts and builds with stone
a bridge over a moat that can be raised to block the way in
the strongest inner tower of a castle, used as a last defense

plate.alt: An old painting of a tall golden stone building going up, with workers cutting stone blocks on the ground and a big wooden wheel crane on top
plate.credit: Construction of the Temple of Jerusalem, Josephus, Antiquités judaïques (Français 247, fol. 163) · Jean Fouquet, about 1470–1475 · Bibliothèque nationale de France · Public domain
plate.look: A painting by Jean Fouquet, made in France about 550 years ago. It tells a very old story about building a temple, but Fouquet painted the builders the way workers built in his own time. At the bottom, masons shape blocks of stone with hammers and chisels. At the very top, a big wooden wheel works as a crane to lift the heavy stones.

mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. A cause is why something happens. The effect is what happens. Castle builders did everything for a reason, and the article tells you why. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.script: [curious] What do a letter, a story, and a grocery list have in common? Somebody wrote them! There's a root that means write, and it has two spellings. Script. And scribe. Here's a word that's not on your list. Postscript. Post means after. So a postscript is writing you add after a letter: P.S.! Read the four words and think about the questions. Then tap See if you cracked it, and type the missing parts.

mods.script: Be a word detective with me. Battlements. Here's a sentence. The archers hid behind the battlements at the top of the wall. They hid behind them, up on top of the wall. So battlements must be the bumpy stone edge on top of a castle wall. One, read the sentence. Two, look for word parts. Three, check that the meaning fits. Now fill in each sentence from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.

mods.todo: Tap Now check your thinking. Then sort each sentence: main idea, detail, or off the topic.
mods.script: [warmly] Think of a paragraph like a table. The main idea is the tabletop. The details are the legs that hold it up. Listen. Knights trained hard. They practiced with swords. They rode horses every day. Knights trained hard is the main idea. The other two hold it up. And I like pizza? That's off the topic. Read the paragraph, and tap Now check your thinking. Then sort each sentence: main idea, detail, or off the topic.

mods.script: Say these with me. Painful. Painless. Same base word: pain. Ful means full of, so painful is full of pain. Less means without. Now two more jobs. Calm, calmness. Ness turns a describing word into a thing. Calm, calmly. Ly tells how something was done. Say the words in Group A and Group B, and tap See the Rule. Then sort all eight words.

virtue.name: diligence
virtue.title: Diligence Watch: Is someone working hard?

items.t: Hundreds of workers worked on the castle site every day.
items.why: They kept working, day after day, on one huge job.

items.t: A drawbridge could be raised to block the entrance.
items.why: That is a fact about the castle, not about someone working.

items.t: Workers kept building one big castle for many years, and some took more than thirty.
items.why: Sticking with one job for years is diligence.
